schema_note: An INSTANCE artifact over the model's configuration layer (../../model/council.json). A configuration is a type; a charter is a seated council. DECLARED = the engine cannot derive it; DERIVED = shown for the reader, binds nothing. Rules the SERVER owns are REFERENCED by name and version, never restated (feedback-2 §1: a restated invariant drifted from its source within eight minutes). The overlay uses four ops the model does not yet define — declare_param, add_motion, patch-with-add, restrict_actions.scope — proposed in ../model-defects.md F1/F3/F10/F14; a loader built from council.json as written would reject this charter until they land. ../tools/check-charter.py checks it against the model plus those four ops.

discharge; bare majority if the reporting deadline was missed or while a partial report is under consideration

read the whole record, including debate and per-seat votes — a DECLARED DEPARTURE from the committee default, under which what occurred in a committee's deliberations is not alluded to except by its report or unanimous consent [51:65]; 49:19 (a conditioned power over a board's minutes) does not supply this entitlement (feedback-2 §4)

authority.DERIVED_on_report: deciders: council seats under delegated authority (grant); decided-by: delegated until the parent acts

roll.desc: DECLARED. A perspective names what the seat LOOKS AT. `slot` is the roster slot the server's lottery keys on (contention rev 3 F3) — assigned here at seating, never by name or join order. Identities (feedback-1 §12, feedback-2 §9): COUNTING identity is the seat; ACCOUNTABILITY identity is the fork key that acted; for the 'present or notified' tests of 35:2(7)/37:35(3) the SEAT stands in for the fork keys that voted (counting identity governs presence tests); a seat's recorded vote binds its occupant for the rest of the session (re-forking within a session does not clear losing-side status); across sessions the occupant is 'absent' under 37:35(2). CONTINUITY of judgment is not asserted.

seats.perspective: the tool's invariants: what the event trail can and cannot say; what a typed field costs to keep true
what a reader sees who opens the file without the tool: grep, GitHub, a fresh agent
the commit seam: worktrees, rebases, hashes cited as evidence

officers.chair_desc: the server performs chair duties under duty_sequencing; on judgment predicates it RULES THE DEFAULT (germane true, dilatory false, substantially-same false, …) and SUBMITS to the council [23:18-21] only when a seat raises the point or the predicate has no default (privilege-admissible, divisible). Costs, named (feedback-2 §9): the sua-sponte duties are lost (dilatory 39, 13:9; decorum 43; denying recognition 50:25 n7); and every contested judgment goes straight to a majority vote, so a 2–1 bloc decides every germaneness, dilatoriness and same-question ruling — the minority loses the protection of a neutral ruling that needs a majority to overturn and is sustained on a tie [24:3(7)]. A mechanical chair is not a member and never votes.

quorum.cite: 40:5 (2 of 3). On a 1- or 2-seat council a majority is the whole roll and one silent seat blocks every vote round at the backstop; the checker warns (feedback-2 §8)

agenda.DERIVED: the referred subject is the special order for the meeting [41:57]; nothing else may be taken up except what arises from it [9:15 by analogy]; the council may report or ask instructions [52:15], never amend this

instructions.desc: DECLARED, binding [13:8(d)]. Numeric bounds are declare_param'd once and referenced from expressions.

list.value: the report — charge, facts, findings, recommendation as a resolution [51:7] — is TEXT THE COUNCIL ADOPTS: it is the content of the motion to rise and report, debatable and amendable as to that text, so that it 'contain[s] only what has been agreed to by a majority vote' [51:2] (feedback-2 §4). Per-seat votes on the record [48:5(2c)] with a pointer to that seat's debate statements; minority views are held to the same pointer rule (a view is a pointer to statements made where they could be answered), not post-vote text

the report carries the label 'majority report of a council run under the contention-rounds discipline; by 9:34's letter a presentation made upon separate consultation [51:2], described thus' — a labeling rule on the report rather than a validity claim (feedback-2 §11)

the final vote on the recommendation, and rising while the referred question is undisposed, are out of order until every seat on the roll has been ASKED in at least one closed debate round on the question since the roll last changed — opportunity, as 49:16 states it; a seat that was asked and stayed silent had its opportunity (feedback-2 §2.2)
requires_schema: presence-history: an asked/answered record per seat per round (F15)

list.conditions: two-thirds; the stated perspective must not already be on the roll (a point of order routes the judgment); a seat added while a question is pending does not vote on it — it votes only on questions stated after its seating (feedback-2 §2.3)

motion.name: Rise and Report
params: report (the text: charge, facts, findings, recommendation as a resolution)

applies_to.desc: carries the report's text as its content; debatable and amendable as to that text, so what is reported is what a majority agreed [51:2]; reached through action/move

out_of_order_when.desc: PROVISIONAL (feedback-2 §2.1 replaced the vacuous floor-claims predicate; the exact form may move with the debate-mode decision): while the referred question is undisposed, rising is out of order until every seat has been asked in a closed debate round on it — so two seats cannot end the council before the third was heard
out_of_order_when.cite: 50:23 (rise only when ready to go out of existence), 49:16

motion.effect: emit the adopted text to the parent as event `reported` (the model's own vocabulary; 'adopted' is the parent's act [51:10-14]); the council dissolves [50:10, 36:8]

motion.name: Engage a Consultant

applies_to.desc: in order whether or not a question is pending; does not touch the pending stack; creates NO subcommittee (50:15) — a consultant has no roll, quorum or charter

requires_schema: ctx.consultants — a list of engaged consultant tasks {id, brief, state}; lighter than committee-identity, which this motion no longer needs
motion.effect: fork the consultant with the brief; its return arrives as event `consultant-reported` and attaches to the pending question as an advisory input, in the nature of debate [52:28] — gating nothing. DECLARED departure: 52:28's breakout groups meet during a recess. Without this instruction the council can only ask the parent [13:22, 52:15].
motion.nonmember_rule: the consultant is a nonmember: it participates only by its return, never in rounds [9:36 last item; 61:7]; it keeps its own tools; the council store is isolated from it as from members (electronic_meeting_rules.equipment)

motion.name: Co-opt a Member
params: perspective (what the seat looks at; must not already be on the roll)

applies_to.desc: in order whether or not a question is pending; classed incidental by this charter (its book analogy, a question of privilege of the assembly's organization [19:7], would be rank 10 — the analogy is not relied on for class)

motion.effect: seat-member: credential; event `member-seated`; membership_total incremented; quorum recomputed [40:5]; fresh counters; the new seat votes only on questions stated after its seating (DECLARED; a conjunct on `vote` keyed to the seat's seating round — requires seat-time in presence history, F15); removal is by the thresholds for rescinding something adopted — in a committee two-thirds, or a majority when every seat that voted for the addition is present or notified [50:14, 35:2(7)] (revision 2 said 'mirrors the adoption threshold'; wrong). Packing is bounded by two-thirds, the distinct-perspective rule, and the no-vote-on-pending-questions rule (feedback-2 §2.3); the parent may add ratification-before-voting by instruction.

electronic_meeting_rules.cite: 9:35-36. DECLARED DEPARTURE from 9:34's letter (01 §4); the report carries the label under instruction report-label.
electronic_meeting_rules.server_discipline: REFERENCED: contention-rounds rev 3 (parliamentary_authority.server_rules) — F1 order-independence; F2 universal opportunity at round-open states; F3 equivariance except least-recently-given-the-floor, the committed-seed lottery keyed by floor-grant count and roster slot, and the slot as last tie-break; F4 one clock door; I1 informed FLOOR acts (non-floor acts in a round are blind to each other by design); IND independence of losing claims; S sealing. Not restated here; this section carries only what varies per council.
electronic_meeting_rules.equipment: the council store is isolated from every seat and every consultant (filesystem permission on the store, not withholding of tools — a seat whose perspective is 're-derive, don't remember' needs its tools; feedback-2 §5 [guess at mechanism]); sealed intents live where nothing but the server reads them (property S)
electronic_meeting_rules.nonmembers: a consultant participates only by its return; the parent participates only by instruction and by reading the record; no nonmember submits in a round [9:36 last item, 61:7]
electronic_meeting_rules.notice: the call of each sitting names the round backstop, the store location, and these rules [9:36; Sample Rules A §1]
electronic_meeting_rules.presence_and_quorum: roll round at call to order; maintained by answering; the backstop marks a seat absent for the round and records that it was ASKED; continued quorum presumed [40:12]
electronic_meeting_rules.quorum_doubt: any seat, any round; the server counts
electronic_meeting_rules.recognition: per contention rev 3 §4 step 6: maker's first speech [42:9(1)] → least-recently-given-the-floor → the lottery. (Revision 2 carried the retracted claim-age rule.)
electronic_meeting_rules.motions_in_writing: written; the maker's modify/withdraw window [4:19] costs one targeted round between made and stated (contention §8) — PARKED (serial-floor finding) whether this council spends it or declares the window dropped
electronic_meeting_rules.debate_mode: PARKED: serial (the model's floor machinery) or rounds in which every seat speaks (the higher-council shape, ../../../high-councils/higher-council-principles.md); see ../reaction-higher-councils.md
electronic_meeting_rules.voting: a signed ballot [45:46]: one final ballot per seat per vote round, recorded per seat, revealed at close; classified `roll-call` for `prevailing_members`; no change (change-vote disabled; a vote round closes at its deadline and a seat slower than it loses its ballot — contention F4's declared residue; this council's remedy: deadline length DECLARED in notice); the chair never votes; unanimous consent by a consent round, any objection defeats it [4:59]
electronic_meeting_rules.duty_sequencing: derived chair events fire only at round boundaries, on the strength of answers never of silence (contention §4 step 7); put-question only after a closed round in which no present seat claimed the floor for debate, following the stating of the question or the last speech (F11)

backstop.wall_clock: DECLARED per sitting in the notice
backstop.recorded_as: a fact on round-closed, with the asked/answered record

malfunction.effect: absent for the round, never penalized; a late response is logged and not applied; silence never puts a question and never kills a motion; a vote round still closes (contention F4, rev 3)

electronic_meeting_rules.polling_fallback: without the round discipline the council may report only what every seat agreed to [51:2]
